title: Reading Drill — Measuring a pond's change in level — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Measuring a pond's change in level — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Brackenton, work on still water on the shore hiding a slow rise had already produced a small collection of a gauge board. The park ecologist used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: water depth beside the outlet.

**B** The group kept readings at fixed intervals for the new trial, which was planned to run for six weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that recent watering nearby should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
